421: Fraudulent procurement of Ennis's COLORWORX registration; Board granted summary judgment dismissing the fraud-based cancellation claim, and the court affirmed because Beling showed no evidence that Ennis knew of confusingly similar marks or intended to deceive the PTO.

Because Mr. Beling did not produce evidence that Ennis actually knew of a confusingly similar third-party mark or intended to deceive the PTO, we affirm the Board's grant of summary judgment on the fraudulent procurement claim.
716: Abandonment counterclaim: whether New Millennium abandoned its KELME registration by using a modernized version of the mark; court held no abandonment, so registration kept.
We agree with the Board that New Millennium did not abandon its registered mark.
908: Cancellation of a Supplemental Register service mark registration: the Board cancelled the registration because the underlying application was void ab initio for nonuse and non-ownership of the mark at filing; affirmed.
Thus, registration by one who did not own the mark at the time of filing renders the underlying application void ab initio.
1013: Cancellation for abandonment/nonuse: whether JobDiva's marks were used for personnel placement and recruitment services, or only for software. The court held the Board applied the wrong legal standard and vacated the nonuse-based cancellation.
Because the Board applied the wrong legal standard, we vacate its judgment and remand for further consideration in light of this opinion.
1127: Cancellation of ECC's registration of THE EMERALD CITY because the pre-registration 2009 agreement was an immediate assignment of an intent-to-use application in violation of the Lanham Act §10 anti-trafficking rule (15 U.S.C. §1060(a)(1)).

Accordingly, we conclude that the Agreement, when read in its entirety, unambiguously shows that, by virtue of its execution, ECC acquired, and Orlando relinquished, immediate control and ownership of the intent-to-use application
3355: Cancellation for nonuse: whether the Church's February 2005 sale of two marked hats to an out-of-state resident satisfied the 'use in commerce' requirement before registration, so the Board erred in cancelling the registrations; the court held intrastate sales to out-of-state residents can constitute use in commerce and rejected the de minimis rationale.

we reverse the Board's cancellation of the Church's "ADD A ZERO" marks for not using them in commerce before federally registering them and remand for the Board to address Adidas's other cancellation grounds.
3849: Cancellation of Registration No. 3788757 for the FUSION mark for abandonment based on three or more consecutive years of nonuse; TTAB found prima facie abandonment not rebutted, and the court held substantial evidence supported the finding.
Substantial evidence supports the TTAB’s finding that CP had not used or intended to resume use of the FUSION mark for at least three consecutive years.
6531: Cancellation for fraud on the PTO based on the Section 2(f) substantially exclusive use averment; the Board's falsity analysis was legally erroneous and the fraud issue was remanded without a final outcome.
Accordingly, we vacate the portion of the Board's decision concerning fraud, and remand for further consideration consistent with this opinion.
7919: Cancellation of the Schiedmayer registration; the Board's order cancelling the registration was upheld.
We uphold the decision of the Board canceling Sweet 16's registration.
8540: Cancellation of registration for BF-7 mark on the ground that Sunbio was not the owner at filing because it had not used the mark in commerce (non-use), including substantial-evidence review of ownership and related-company attribution of SmartNutri's use.
we conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Sunbio was not the owner of the BF-7 mark at the time of its trademark registration application, we affirm.
8658: Whether Section 14 of the Lanham Act permits the Board to cancel a registration based on a fraudulent Section 15 incontestability declaration; the court held it does not and reversed the cancellation.

Because Section 14 does not authorize the Board to cancel a registration based on a fraudulent Section 15 declaration, which is necessarily directed only to obtaining incontestable status of an already-registered mark and does not involve a "registration [that] was obtained fraudulently," we do not reach the issue of whether the Board erred in finding that Mr. Taylor committed fraud.
8868: Whether Section 14 authorizes the Board to cancel a registration based on a fraudulent Section 15 incontestability declaration; the court held it does not and reversed the cancellation.
We conclude, however, that Section 14 does not permit the Board to cancel a registration in these circumstances.
10406: Cancellation of the registration for failure to use the mark in commerce before the filing date (nonuse ground)
Because we find no error in the Board's determination that Mr. Ghomeshi failed to show use of the mark in commerce prior to applying for registration, we affirm.
11210: Fraud cancellation ground: the Board erred in requiring Galperti-USA to show secondary meaning (proprietary rights) in its own use of GALPERTI for that use to count in showing falsity of the substantially-exclusive-use claim; the court vacated and remanded on the falsity analysis.

Contrary to the Board's ruling, therefore, we conclude that Galperti-USA does not need to establish secondary meaning of its own uses of GALPERTI in order for those uses to be counted in determining the falsity of Galperti-Italy's claim of substantially exclusive use.
11211: Fraud cancellation ground: the Board erred in requiring privity between Galperti-USA and third-party users before third-party use could be counted in showing falsity of the substantially-exclusive-use claim; the court vacated and remanded.
Use by anyone, regardless of relation to the challenger, may undercut a claim of substantially exclusive use.
11412: Cancellation grounds: priority of use under § 1052(d) supporting cancellation of the '672 registration; court held substantial evidence supported Narita Export's priority of use based on acquired common-law rights.
We therefore conclude that the Board's priority of use decision was supported by substantial evidence.
13990: Cancellation of registrations: Brittex's §2(d) priority-based cancellation resulted in partial cancellation of the pawn brokerage and pawn shop services from DFG's registrations.
The Board accordingly partially granted the petition for cancellation and required "[p]awn brokerage and pawn shops" be deleted from Registration Nos. 4,524,540 and 4,532,073.
14563: Cancellation of Game Plan's registration under Section 2(d) priority counterclaim based on UNIP's acquired common law rights; registration cancelled.
The Board accordingly held that UNIP had priority over Game Plan and canceled Game Plan's registration.
